title: India updates rules to clear FDI proposals within 12 weeks
summary:
India has revised its FDI approval process, extending the decision timeline to 12 weeks from 10 weeks earlier under a new DPIIT framework. 
Investments from neighbouring countries will require Ministry of External Affairs clearance. 
The government also eased norms for firms with up to 10 per cent Chinese/Hong Kong shareholding and introduced 60-day fast-track approvals for a few sectors.

title: Indian court stays rollback of QCOs for FDY, POY yarns
summary:
The Gujarat High Court has stayed the withdrawal of Quality Control Orders (QCOs) for FDY and POY, granting interim relief to Sumeet Industries Limited. 
The court directed that the QCOs will remain in force until further hearing. 
Industry sources said the government may challenge the order amid concerns over raw material availability, and rising input costs in India’s textile sector.

title: India approves $595 mn cotton mission as supply tightens
summary:
India approved a $595 million cotton productivity mission for 2026-31 to boost yields, quality and self-sufficiency amid rising cotton and yarn prices, tight domestic supply, and higher exports.
The plan focuses on better seeds, modern farming, traceability and processing, targeting higher output, improved productivity, and stronger global competitiveness.

title: ICE cotton extends rally on dry weather, crude oil surge
summary:
ICE cotton futures surged to fresh multi-month highs as dry weather in West Texas, elevated crude oil prices and supportive macroeconomic sentiment boosted buying interest.
Rising polyester costs improved cotton’s competitiveness against man-made fibres, while geopolitical risks and expectations of renewed Chinese participation continued to support overall market sentiment.

title: Uzbekistan, Tajikistan boost trade facilitation on Trans-Caspian route
summary:
Uzbekistan and Tajikistan advanced trade facilitation by progressing toward electronic exchange of certificates of origin under an EU-backed project. 
A technical meeting in Tashkent focused on data standards, protocols and system integration. 
The initiative aims to cut delays, boost transparency and strengthen connectivity along the Trans-Caspian route.

title: ASEAN manufacturing momentum eases in April amid rising cost pressures
summary:
ASEAN manufacturing growth slowed in April, with the S&P Global Manufacturing PMI falling to a nine-month low of 50.7. 
Output and new orders weakened, export sales declined further, and employment fell for the first time in eight months. 
Supply chain pressures and rising operating costs intensified inflation. 
Despite weaker momentum, firms remained optimistic.

title: US sanctions hit Turkish textile trade, trigger compliance risk surge
summary:
OFAC’s April 21 strike on Esenyurt’s Emti Fiber Textile, a 30-month-old cotton-linter trader feeding Iran's missile chain, has rewritten Turkish textile compliance overnight. 
Turkiye’s $26.18 billion sector fell 4.4 per cent in 2025 as EU buyers shifted to China (+22.3%), Bangladesh (+17.9%), Vietnam (+17.3%); Turkiye alone slipped 5.8 per cent. 
Brand vendor purges hit May 5-12.

title: UK manufacturing index climbs to 4-year high in April
summary:
UK manufacturing PMI rose to 53.7 in April, a near four-year high, marking six months of expansion. 
Output, new orders, and employment improved, but supply chain disruptions, linked to Middle East tensions drove delays and sharp cost increases. 
Firms raised prices and boosted purchasing to hedge risks.However, optimism weakened, and growth may slow later.

title: Australia’s central bank raises rates as inflation pressures persist
summary:
The Reserve Bank of Australia has raised its cash rate by 25 bps to 4.35 per cent, citing persistent inflation and Middle East-driven energy price risks. 
Inflation rose in late 2025 and may peak higher before easing. 
Financial conditions have tightened, though credit remains available. 
The RBA warned of uncertainty and possible second-round effects and expects inflation to stay above target.

title: Moody's raises Vietnam's outlook to ‘positive’ from ‘stable’
summary:
Moody's Ratings recently raised its outlook on Vietnam to ‘positive’ from ‘stable’, citing rising confidence in the country's ability to strengthen its credit profile over the medium term. 
Affirming its ⁠’Ba2’ rating, it said Vietnam's institutional quality and governance were improving due to reforms implemented since late-2024, and downside risks from US trade measures had relatively eased.

title: China loses 4% Canada apparel market share as western buyers diversify
summary:
Canada’s apparel sourcing is shifting as China’s share fell over 4 per cent to 25.5 per cent in January-February 2026, with exports dropping sharply.
Bangladesh, Vietnam, and Cambodia gained share, while India saw a marginal rise.
Total imports dipped to $1.71 billion.
The trend reflects diversification amid cost pressures, geopolitics, and trade advantages for rival suppliers.

title: Bangladesh’s cumulative RMG exports down, but rebound in April
summary:
Bangladesh’s RMG exports saw a modest 2.82 per cent decline in FY26 (July–April), led by weaker knitwear.
Woven garments showed relatively better resilience, while home textiles posted marginal growth.
April marked a sharp rebound, with strong YoY gains across apparel and home segments.
Despite volatility, textiles remain dominant, contributing over 82 per cent of total exports.

title: US’ Carter’s taps retail veteran Sharon Price John as new CEO
summary:
Carter’s, Inc. appointed Sharon Price John as CEO & president effective June 15, 2026, succeeding Douglas C. Palladini. 
Richard F. Westenberger will serve as interim CEO. 
John, ex-Build-A-Bear Workshop chief, drove profitability, omnichannel growth and brand transformation; she also joins the board. 
Carter’s reaffirmed FY26 outlook, amid leadership transition and strategic reset.

title: US’ Brooks Running posts strong Q1 growth on global demand
summary:
Brooks Running has reported strong Q1 2026 growth, with sales rising 20 per cent in North America, 30 per cent in EMEA and 136 per cent in China. 
Growth was driven by footwear innovation and expanding apparel demand. 
The brand-maintained US leadership in performance running footwear and strengthened global presence through new launches, partnerships and athlete performances.

title: Bangladesh’s $4 bn April rebound runs into the LDC clock
summary:
Bangladesh’s $4.01 billion garment exports in April (+33% YoY) is base-effect optics, with Eid-ul-Fitr 2025’s ten production-day shutdown flattering the comparison. 
The real cliff is the November 2029 EBA expiry, not the 2026 LDC graduation; the WTO’s modelled hit is $5.37 billion, not the $8 billion figure Dhaka quotes. 
The US zero-tariff carve-out is volume-quota, not cotton-content.

title: Epic Group inaugurates Trimetro manufacturing campus in Odisha
summary:
Epic Group has inaugurated its $100 million Trimetro campus in Odisha, India’s first garment facility to achieve both net-zero carbon and net-zero water status. 
Spread across 40 acres, it will produce 20 million garments annually while generating 10,000 jobs, with 80 per cent women workforce, setting a benchmark in sustainable, inclusive manufacturing.

title: South Korea’s apparel imports down to $3 bn, March sees sharper dip
summary:
South Korea’s apparel imports edged down 1.21 per cent to $3.02 billion in Q1 2026, with March imports dropping sharply by 11.9 per cent.
Knitted imports rose slightly, while non-knitted declined.
Textile exports also fell amid weak global demand and rising competition.
The country continues to rely on garment imports while exporting fabrics and materials.

title: How recent wage hike put India’s NCR T&A sector to test
summary:
Sharp wage hikes are triggering a cost shock, severely squeezing margins for NCR textile and apparel manufacturers. 
MSMEs are most vulnerable, with rising labour costs threatening financial stability and operations. 
Industry fears loss of competitiveness. 
Unrest and policy uncertainty risk damaging NCR’s credibility as a reliable manufacturing hub.

title: Brazil’s apparel imports double in 5 years, momentum persists
summary:
Brazil’s apparel imports have more than doubled in five years, with 2026 maintaining strong momentum.
Q1 alone accounts for nearly one-third of 2025’s total, signalling potential record highs.
Growth is driven by resilient demand and rising import dependence, with a clear shift towards affordable, high-volume basics like T-shirts over premium segments.

title: US’ Crocs' Q1 strong on DTC growth; margins, EPS decline
summary:
Crocs has reported better-than-expected Q1 2026 results, with revenue at $921 million, down 1.7 per cent, driven by 12.1 per cent DTC growth.  Gross margin fell to 56.8 per cent, while EPS dipped to $2.71. 
The Crocs brand grew modestly, but HEYDUDE declined.
